NKJV.2: “Hear my words, you wise men; Give ear to me, you who have knowledge.
NKJV.3: For the ear tests words As the palate tastes food.
NKJV.4: Let us choose justice for ourselves; Let us know among ourselves what is good.
NKJV.5: “For Job has said, ‘I am righteous, But God has taken away my justice;
NKJV.6: Should I lie concerning my right? My wound is incurable, though I am without transgression.’
NKJV.7: What man is like Job, Who drinks scorn like water,
NKJV.8: Who goes in company with the workers of iniquity, And walks with wicked men?
NKJV.9: For he has said, ‘It profits a man nothing That he should delight in God.’
NKJV.10: “Therefore listen to me, you men of understanding: Far be it from God to do wickedness, And from the Almighty to commit iniquity.
NKJV.11: For He repays man according to his work, And makes man to find a reward according to his way.
NKJV.12: Surely God will never do wickedly, Nor will the Almighty pervert justice.
NKJV.13: Who gave Him charge over the earth? Or who appointed Him over the whole world?
NKJV.14: If He should set His heart on it, If He should gather to Himself His Spirit and His breath,
NKJV.15: All flesh would perish together, And man would return to dust.
NKJV.16: “If you have understanding, hear this; Listen to the sound of my words:
NKJV.17: Should one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn Him who is most just?
NKJV.18: Is it fitting to say to a king, ‘You are worthless,’ And to nobles, ‘You are wicked’?
NKJV.19: Yet He is not partial to princes, Nor does He regard the rich more than the poor; For they are all the work of His hands.
NKJV.20: In a moment they die, in the middle of the night; The people are shaken and pass away; The mighty are taken away without a hand.
NKJV.21: “For His eyes are on the ways of man, And He sees all his steps.
NKJV.22: There is no darkness nor shadow of death Where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.
NKJV.23: For He need not further consider a man, That he should go before God in judgment.
NKJV.24: He breaks in pieces mighty men without inquiry, And sets others in their place.
NKJV.25: Therefore He knows their works; He overthrows them in the night, And they are crushed.
NKJV.26: He strikes them as wicked men In the open sight of others,
NKJV.27: Because they turned back from Him, And would not consider any of His ways,
NKJV.28: So that they caused the cry of the poor to come to Him; For He hears the cry of the afflicted.
NKJV.29: When He gives quietness, who then can make trouble? And when He hides His face, who then can see Him, Whether it is against a nation or a man alone?—
NKJV.30: That the hypocrite should not reign, Lest the people be ensnared.
NKJV.31: “For has anyone said to God, ‘I have borne chastening; I will offend no more;
NKJV.32: Teach me what I do not see; If I have done iniquity, I will do no more’?
NKJV.33: Should He repay it according to your terms, Just because you disavow it? You must choose, and not I; Therefore speak what you know.
NKJV.34: “Men of understanding say to me, Wise men who listen to me:
NKJV.35: ‘Job speaks without knowledge, His words are without wisdom.’
NKJV.36: Oh, that Job were tried to the utmost, Because his answers are like those of wicked men!
NKJV.37: For he adds rebellion to his sin; He claps his hands among us, And multiplies his words against God.”

NASB.21: 'For His eyes are upon the ways of a man, And He sees all his steps.
NASB.22: 'There is no darkness or deep shadow Where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.
NASB.23: 'For He does not [need to] consider a man further, That he should go before God in judgment.

ESV.2: “Hear my words, you wise men, and give ear to me, you who know;
ESV.3: for the ear tests words as the palate tastes food.
ESV.4: Let us choose what is right; let us know among ourselves what is good.
ESV.5: For Job has said, ‘I am in the right, and God has taken away my right;
ESV.6: in spite of my right I am counted a liar; my wound is incurable, though I am without transgression.’
ESV.7: What man is like Job, who drinks up scoffing like water,
ESV.8: who travels in company with evildoers and walks with wicked men?
ESV.9: For he has said, ‘It profits a man nothing that he should take delight in God.’
ESV.10: “Therefore, hear me, you men of understanding: far be it from God that he should do wickedness, and from the Almighty that he should do wrong.
ESV.11: For according to the work of a man he will repay him, and according to his ways he will make it befall him.
ESV.12: Of a truth, God will not do wickedly, and the Almighty will not pervert justice.
ESV.13: Who gave him charge over the earth, and who laid on him  the whole world?
ESV.14: If he should set his heart to it and gather to himself his spirit and his breath,
ESV.15: all flesh would perish together, and man would return to dust.
ESV.16: “If you have understanding, hear this; listen to what I say.
ESV.17: Shall one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn him who is righteous and mighty,
ESV.18: who says to a king, ‘Worthless one,’ and to nobles, ‘Wicked man,’
ESV.19: who shows no partiality to princes, nor regards the rich more than the poor, for they are all the work of his hands?
ESV.20: In a moment they die; at midnight the people are shaken and pass away, and the mighty are taken away by no human hand.
ESV.21: “For his eyes are on the ways of a man, and he sees all his steps.
ESV.22: There is no gloom or deep darkness where evildoers may hide themselves.
ESV.23: For God  has no need to consider a man further, that he should go before God in judgment.
ESV.24: He shatters the mighty without investigation and sets others in their place.
ESV.25: Thus, knowing their works, he overturns them in the night, and they are crushed.
ESV.26: He strikes them for their wickedness in a place for all to see,
ESV.27: because they turned aside from following him and had no regard for any of his ways,
ESV.28: so that they caused the cry of the poor to come to him, and he heard the cry of the afflicted —
ESV.29: When he is quiet, who can condemn? When he hides his face, who can behold him, whether it be a nation or a man? —
ESV.30: that a godless man should not reign, that he should not ensnare the people.
ESV.31: “For has anyone said to God, ‘I have borne punishment; I will not offend any more;
ESV.32: teach me what I do not see; if I have done iniquity, I will do it no more’?
ESV.33: Will he then make repayment to suit you, because you reject it? For you must choose, and not I; therefore declare what you know.
ESV.34: Men of understanding will say to me, and the wise man who hears me will say:
ESV.35: ‘Job speaks without knowledge; his words are without insight.’
ESV.36: Would that Job were tried to the end, because he answers like wicked men.
ESV.37: For he adds rebellion to his sin; he claps his hands among us and multiplies his words against God.”

Hear my words, you wise ones,
and listen to me, you knowledgeable ones.
CSB17.3:
Doesn’t the ear test words
as the palate tastes food?
CSB17.4:
Let us judge for ourselves what is right;
let us decide together what is good.
CSB17.5:
For Job has declared, “I am righteous,
yet God has deprived me of justice. ⓔ
CSB17.6:
Would I lie about my case? ⓕ
My wound [2] is incurable,
though I am without transgression.”
CSB17.7:
What man is like Job?
He drinks derision ⓖ like water.
CSB17.8:
He keeps company with evildoers
and walks with wicked men.
CSB17.9:
For he has said, “A man gains nothing
when he becomes God’s friend.” ⓗ
CSB17.10:
Therefore listen to me, you men of understanding.
It is impossible for God to do wrong,
and for the Almighty to act unjustly. ⓘ
CSB17.11:
For he repays ⓙ a person according to his deeds,
and he gives him what his conduct deserves. [3]
CSB17.12:
Indeed, it is true that God does not act wickedly
and the Almighty does not pervert justice. ⓚ
CSB17.13:
Who gave him authority over the earth?
Who put him in charge of the entire world? ⓛ
CSB17.14:
If he put his mind to it
and withdrew the spirit ⓜ and breath he gave,
CSB17.15:
every living thing would perish together
and mankind would return to the dust. ⓝ
CSB17.16:
If you have understanding, hear this;
listen to what I have to say.
CSB17.17:
Could one who hates justice govern the world?
Will you condemn the mighty Righteous One, ⓐ
CSB17.18:
who says to a king, “Worthless man!”
and to nobles, “Wicked men!”? ⓑ
CSB17.19:
God is not partial ⓒ to princes
and does not favor the rich over the poor,
for they are all the work of his hands.
CSB17.20:
They die suddenly in the middle of the night;
people shudder, then pass away.
Even the mighty are removed without effort.
CSB17.21:
For his eyes watch over a man’s ways,
and he observes all his steps. ⓓ
CSB17.22:
There is no darkness, no deep darkness,
where evildoers can hide. ⓔ
CSB17.23:
God does not need to examine a person further,
that one should [4] approach him in court.
CSB17.24:
He shatters the mighty without an investigation
and sets others in their place. ⓕ
CSB17.25:
Therefore, he recognizes their deeds ⓖ
and overthrows them by night, and they are crushed.
CSB17.26:
In full view of the public, [5]
he strikes them for their wickedness,
CSB17.27:
because they turned aside from following him
and did not understand any of his ways
CSB17.28:
but caused the poor to cry out to him,
and he heard the outcry of the needy. ⓗ
CSB17.29:
But when God is silent, who can declare him guilty?
When he hides his face, who can see him?
Yet he watches over both individuals and nations,
CSB17.30:
so that godless men should not rule
or ensnare the people.
CSB17.31:
Suppose someone says to God,
“I have endured my punishment;
I will no longer act wickedly.
CSB17.32:
Teach me what I cannot see;
if I have done wrong, I won’t do it again.”
CSB17.33:
Should God repay you on your terms
when you have rejected his?
You must choose, not I!
So declare what you know.
CSB17.34:
Reasonable men will say to me,
along with the wise men who hear me,
CSB17.35:
“Job speaks without knowledge; ⓘ
his words are without insight.”
CSB17.36:
If only Job were tested to the limit,
because his answers are like those of wicked men.
CSB17.37:
For he adds rebellion to his sin;
he scornfully claps ⓙ in our presence,
while multiplying ⓚ his words against God.

NLT.2:
“Listen to me, you wise men.
Pay attention, you who have knowledge.
NLT.3:
Job said, ‘The ear tests the words it hears
just as the mouth distinguishes between foods.’
NLT.4:
So let us discern for ourselves what is right;
let us learn together what is good.
NLT.5:
For Job also said, ‘I am innocent,
but God has taken away my rights.
NLT.6:
I am innocent, but they call me a liar.
My suffering is incurable, though I have not sinned.’
NLT.7:
“Tell me, has there ever been a man like Job,
with his thirst for irreverent talk?
NLT.8:
He chooses evil people as companions.
He spends his time with wicked men.
NLT.9:
He has even said, ‘Why waste time
trying to please God?’
NLT.10:
“Listen to me, you who have understanding.
Everyone knows that God doesn’t sin!
The Almighty can do no wrong.
NLT.11:
He repays people according to their deeds.
He treats people as they deserve.
NLT.12:
Truly, God will not do wrong.
The Almighty will not twist justice.
NLT.13:
Did someone else put the world in his care?
Who set the whole world in place?
NLT.14:
If God were to take back his spirit
and withdraw his breath,
NLT.15:
all life would cease,
and humanity would turn again to dust.
NLT.16:
“Now listen to me if you are wise.
Pay attention to what I say.
NLT.17:
Could God govern if he hated justice?
Are you going to condemn the almighty judge?
NLT.18:
For he says to kings, ‘You are wicked,’
and to nobles, ‘You are unjust.’
NLT.19:
He doesn’t care how great a person may be,
and he pays no more attention to the rich than to the poor.
He made them all.
NLT.20:
In a moment they die.
In the middle of the night they pass away;
the mighty are removed without human hand.
NLT.21:
“For God watches how people live;
he sees everything they do.
NLT.22:
No darkness is thick enough
to hide the wicked from his eyes.
NLT.23:
We don’t set the time
when we will come before God in judgment.
NLT.24:
He brings the mighty to ruin without asking anyone,
and he sets up others in their place.
NLT.25:
He knows what they do,
and in the night he overturns and destroys them.
NLT.26:
He strikes them down because they are wicked,
doing it openly for all to see.
NLT.27:
For they turned away from following him.
They have no respect for any of his ways.
NLT.28:
They cause the poor to cry out, catching God’s attention.
He hears the cries of the needy.
NLT.29:
But if he chooses to remain quiet,
who can criticize him?
When he hides his face, no one can find him,
whether an individual or a nation.
NLT.30:
He prevents the godless from ruling
so they cannot be a snare to the people.
NLT.31:
“Why don’t people say to God, ‘I have sinned,
but I will sin no more’?
NLT.32:
Or ‘I don’t know what evil I have done — tell me.
If I have done wrong, I will stop at once’?
NLT.33:
“Must God tailor his justice to your demands?
But you have rejected him!
The choice is yours, not mine.
Go ahead, share your wisdom with us.
NLT.34:
After all, bright people will tell me,
and wise people will hear me say,
NLT.35:
‘Job speaks out of ignorance;
his words lack insight.’
NLT.36:
Job, you deserve the maximum penalty
for the wicked way you have talked.
NLT.37:
For you have added rebellion to your sin;
you show no respect,
and you speak many angry words against God.”

"Let us choose for ourselves that which is right;
Let us know among ourselves what is good.
AMP.5:
"For Job has said, 'I am righteous [and innocent],
But God has taken away my right;
AMP.6:
Although I am right, I am accounted a liar.
My wound is incurable, though I am without transgression.'
AMP.7:
"What man is like Job,
Who drinks up derision like water,
AMP.8:
Who goes in company with those who do evil
And walks with wicked men?
AMP.9:
"For he has said, 'It profits a man nothing
When he takes delight and is pleased with God and obeys Him.'
AMP.10:
"Therefore hear me, you men of understanding.
Far be it from God that He would do wickedness,
And from the Almighty to do wrong.
AMP.11:
"For God pays a man according to his work,
And He will make every man find [appropriate] compensation according to his way.
AMP.12:
"Surely God will not act wickedly,
Nor will the Almighty pervert justice.
AMP.13:
"Who put God in charge over the earth?
And who has laid on Him the whole world?
AMP.14:
"If God should determine to do so,
If He should gather to Himself [that is, withdraw from man] His [life-giving] spirit and His breath,
AMP.15:
All flesh would perish together,
And man would return to dust.
AMP.16:
"If you now have understanding, hear this;
Listen to the sound of my words.
AMP.17:
"Shall one who hates justice [and is an enemy of right] govern?
And will you condemn Him who is just and mighty?
AMP.18:
"God who says to a king, 'You are worthless and vile,'
Or to princes and nobles, 'You are wicked and evil'?
AMP.19:
"Who is not partial to princes,
Nor does He regard the rich above the poor,
For they all are the work of His hands.
AMP.20:
"In a moment they die, even at midnight
The people are shaken and pass away,
And the powerful are taken away without a [human] hand.
AMP.21:
"For God's eyes are on the ways of a man,
And He sees all his steps.
AMP.22:
"There is no darkness nor deep shadow
Where the evildoers may hide themselves.
AMP.23:
"For He sets no appointed time for a man,
That he should appear before Him in judgment.
AMP.24:
"He breaks mighty men without inquiry,
And sets others in their place.
AMP.25:
"Therefore He knows of their works,
And He overthrows them in the night,
So that they are crushed and destroyed.
AMP.26:
"He strikes them like the wicked
In a public place,
AMP.27:
Because they turned aside from following Him
And would not consider or show regard for any of His ways,
AMP.28:
So that they caused the cry of the poor to come to Him,
And He heard the cry of the afflicted.
AMP.29:
"When He keeps quiet, who then can condemn?
When He hides His face [withdrawing His favor and help], who then can behold Him [and make supplication to Him],
Whether it be a nation or a man by himself?—
AMP.30:
So that godless men would not rule
Nor be snares for the people.
AMP.31:
"For has anyone said to God,
'I have endured my chastisement;
I will not offend anymore;
AMP.32:
Teach me what I do not see [in regard to how I have sinned];
If I have done wrong (injustice, unrighteousness),
I will not do it again'?
AMP.33:
"Shall God's retribution [for your sins] be on your terms, because you refuse to accept it?
For you must do the choosing, and not I;
Therefore say what you [truthfully] know.
AMP.34:
"Men of understanding will tell me,
Indeed, every wise man who hears me [will agree],
AMP.35:
'Job speaks without knowledge,
And his words are without wisdom and insight.
AMP.36:
'Job ought to be tried to the limit
Because he answers like wicked men!
AMP.37:
'For he adds rebellion [in his unsubmissive, defiant attitude toward God] to his [unacknowledged] sin;
He claps his hands among us [in open mockery and contempt of God],
And he multiplies his words [of accusation] against God.'"

WEB.2: “Hear my words, you wise men. Give ear to me, you who have knowledge.

WEB.9: For he has said, ‘It profits a man nothing that he should delight himself with God.’
WEB.10: “Therefore listen to me, you men of understanding: far be it from God, that he should do wickedness, from the Almighty, that he should commit iniquity.

WEB.12: Yes surely, God will not do wickedly, neither will the Almighty pervert justice.
WEB.13: Who put him in charge of the earth? or who has appointed him over the whole world?
WEB.14: If he set his heart on himself, If he gathered to himself his spirit and his breath,

WEB.18: Who says to a king, ‘Vile!’ or to nobles, ‘Wicked!’?
WEB.19: Who doesn’t respect the persons of princes, nor respects the rich more than the poor; for they all are the work of his hands.
WEB.20: In a moment they die, even at midnight. The people are shaken and pass away. The mighty are taken away without a hand.
WEB.21: “For his eyes are on the ways of a man. He sees all his goings.
WEB.22: There is no darkness, nor thick gloom, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.
WEB.23: For he doesn’t need to consider a man further, that he should go before God in judgment.

WEB.25: Therefore he takes knowledge of their works. He overturns them in the night, so that they are destroyed.
WEB.26: He strikes them as wicked men in the open sight of others;
WEB.27: because they turned aside from following him, and wouldn’t pay attention to any of his ways,
WEB.28: so that they caused the cry of the poor to come to him. He heard the cry of the afflicted.

WEB.30: that the godless man may not reign, that there be no one to ensnare the people.

WEB.32: Teach me that which I don’t see. If I have done iniquity, I will do it no more’?

WEB.34: Men of understanding will tell me, yes, every wise man who hears me:

MSG.2:
"So, my fine friends—listen to me,
and see what you think of this.
MSG.3:
Isn't it just common sense—
as common as the sense of taste—
MSG.4:
To put our heads together
and figure out what's going on here?
MSG.5:
"We've all heard Job say, 'I'm in the right,
but God won't give me a fair trial.
MSG.6:
When I defend myself, I'm called a liar to my face.
I've done nothing wrong, and I get punished anyway.'
MSG.7:
Have you ever heard anything to beat this?
Does nothing faze this man Job?
MSG.8:
Do you think he's spent too much time in bad company,
hanging out with the wrong crowd,
MSG.9:
So that now he's parroting their line:
'It doesn't pay to try to please God'?
MSG.10:
"You're veterans in dealing with these matters;
certainly we're of one mind on this.
It's impossible for God to do anything evil;
no way can the Mighty One do wrong.
MSG.11:
He makes us pay for exactly what we've done—no more, no less.
Our chickens always come home to roost.
MSG.12:
It's impossible for God to do anything wicked,
for the Mighty One to subvert justice.
MSG.13:
He's the one who runs the earth!
He cradles the whole world in his hand!
MSG.14: If he decided to hold his breath,
MSG.15: every man, woman, and child would die for lack of air.
MSG.16:
"So, Job, use your head;
this is all pretty obvious.
MSG.17:
Can someone who hates order, keep order?
Do you dare condemn the righteous, mighty God?
MSG.18:
Doesn't God always tell it like it is,
exposing corrupt rulers as scoundrels and criminals?
MSG.19:
Does he play favorites with the rich and famous and slight the poor?
Isn't he equally responsible to everybody?
MSG.20:
Don't people who deserve it die without notice?
Don't wicked rulers tumble to their doom?
When the so-called great ones are wiped out,
we know God is working behind the scenes.
MSG.21:
"He has his eyes on every man and woman.
He doesn't miss a trick.
MSG.22:
There is no night dark enough, no shadow deep enough,
to hide those who do evil.
MSG.23:
God doesn't need to gather any more evidence;
their sin is an open-and-shut case.
MSG.24:
He deposes the so-called high and mighty without asking questions,
and replaces them at once with others.
MSG.25:
Nobody gets by with anything; overnight,
judgment is signed, sealed, and delivered.
MSG.26:
He punishes the wicked for their wickedness
out in the open where everyone can see it,
MSG.27:
Because they quit following him,
no longer even thought about him or his ways.
MSG.28:
Their apostasy was announced by the cry of the poor;
the cry of the afflicted got God's attention.
MSG.29:
"If God is silent, what's that to you?
If he turns his face away, what can you do about it?
But whether silent or hidden, he's there, ruling,
MSG.30:
so that those who hate God won't take over
and ruin people's lives.
MSG.31:
"So why don't you simply confess to God?
Say, 'I sinned, but I'll sin no more.
MSG.32:
Teach me to see what I still don't see.
Whatever evil I've done, I'll do it no more.'
MSG.33:
Just because you refuse to live on God's terms,
do you think he should start living on yours?
You choose. I can't do it for you.
Tell me what you decide.
MSG.34:
"All right-thinking people say—
and the wise who have listened to me concur—
MSG.35:
'Job is an ignoramus.
He talks utter nonsense.'
MSG.36:
Job, you need to be pushed to the wall and called to account
for wickedly talking back to God the way you have.
MSG.37:
You've compounded your original sin
by rebelling against God's discipline,
Defiantly shaking your fist at God,
piling up indictments against the Almighty One."
